title: Interfaces and the diamond problem
answer: Interfaces avoid the class-state version of the diamond problem because Java does not inherit instance state from multiple classes. However, default methods can create a behavioral diamond when two parent interfaces provide the same signature. Java resolves this with explicit rules: a more-specific interface wins, otherwise the implementing class or child interface must override and disambiguate.
